decisions.text: RUL40 re-scope: herdr is never a source of truth or a delivery receipt for any fgOS state or Run outcome, but herdr's agent API (agent start / agent prompt --wait / agent wait / agent read / pane process-info) MAY be used by Dispatch as transport and as a failure detector (agent_not_ready, agent_prompt_stalled, blocked, agent absent). Truth stays with fgOS CLI state for Work and with receiver-written files (ack/result in the Run outbox) plus the liveness ladder for Runs. The former absolute ban on calling herdr agent start or reading agent_status is lifted; the ban on treating them as decision truth stays.
decisions.rationale: The 2026-07-18 ban conflated two rules. The measured bug (idle kills agent, airemote) came from trusting idle as completion, not from calling the API. transport.mjs herdrSpawnInteractiveAdapter already reads agent_status as its only completion signal, violating the letter of RUL40 while being unstable (false idle at 3.5s, mid-turn dips ~25%, multi-line prompt corrupting pane run argv). Upstream beegog v2.33.2 proves the stable shape: herdr agent prompt --wait as atomic submit-and-observe, receipt = worker-written ack file, result file outranks every herdr signal, agent liveness from pane process-info. Full investigation: docs/architect/proposals/visibility-and-interactive-contact-herdr-spawn.md sections 3.3, 4, 8, 11, 14 (H1).

decisions.text: Vocabulary: bound-invocation-supervisor (Rust providers::external_process::bound_invocation_supervisor::BoundInvocationSupervisor) vs detached-run-supervisor (Node cli-spawn-supervisor.mjs) -- two process-supervision roles distinguished by the lifecycle/detachment axis, not a content label ('agent' vs 'RPC').
decisions.rationale: supervisor.rs (Rust) and cli-spawn-supervisor.mjs (Node) look like duplicate 'supervisor' implementations (both: bounded capture, deadlines, crash mapping, cancellation grace) but answer different questions. bound-invocation-supervisor runs a short RPC-shaped call bound to ONE invocation's own lifetime, never detached -- confirmed via source: no detach/setsid/process-group logic in supervisor.rs, 2-5s default deadlines. detached-run-supervisor runs a long agent/executor job deliberately DETACHED so it survives the crash of whatever dispatched it -- confirmed via source: cli-spawn-supervisor.mjs's detached spawn, PGID-based kill, immutable receipt publication. Naming by lifecycle (detached+crash-surviving vs bound+caller-lifetime) keeps the names correct if either mechanism's real use case shifts later. Zero live conflict today: the Rust mechanism has zero current consumers (2 native routes -- gate-bypass, version -- neither uses it); dispatch stays 100% legacy-cli. Source: dispatch-engine-liveness-hardening plan.md Phase 8 C4 investigation (invocation_service.rs, operation_provider_router.rs, providers/external_process/*, apps/fgos/src/legacy_exec.rs, docs/platform/host-invocation-routing/architecture/invocation-kernel.md).

decisions.text: D-ADR0055: Event truth is sealed changesets as git objects on per-machine refs -- an event is acknowledged when fsynced in the store's open log outside the work tree and becomes git truth when sealed by compare-and-swap into a commit on refs/fgos/events/<machine-id>; machines share by pushing the own ref and fetching the others; every view is a rebuildable cache. Supersedes L3 clauses 1 and 4 (ae461c8b) and the data layout of D-ADR0003 (tracked events.jsonl, gitignored state.json); L3 clauses 2 and 3 stand. Owner confirmations: machine id owned by Event Store until a machine-identity component exists; non-git directories refused; porting store writes its own project-scope stream; eventStore.sync.intervalSec 300 with opportunistic push; compaction opened when a full rebuild exceeds 2 s on the slowest machine.
decisions.rationale: The event log living in the git work tree caused most git and lock incidents (investigation-261017-1027, git lessons catalogue); spec docs/platform/event-store/spec.md passed council 2, the reopened council, a model check run twice and the V-REF-01 git experiment. Review threshold: a cross-machine conflict resolved by hand more than once a month, or any acknowledged event lost while fgOS was running.

decisions.text: D-ADR0056: Run supervisor in Rust for the direct launch mode -- each attempt has one Rust supervisor (fgos internal supervise) and one launch gate (fgos internal gate) that roots the agent in a provably-empty containment domain (Linux: pid 1 of a PID namespace); the controller holds attempt.lock (+ cwd lease) before any side effect, writes an immutable digest-checked envelope v3, starts the supervisor detached with no pipe and no IPC, and from then only reads receipts from files; a dead supervisor leaves the agent running to exit or the gate's hard ceiling and the adopt door settles from gate-exit.json and the outbox; one door (sweepAttempts/adopt) for resume, recover, the run-start scan and doctor fix; attempt homes carry marker v2. Supersedes the detached-run-supervisor part of D-ADR0043; bound-invocation-supervisor stays.
decisions.rationale: The Node detached-run-supervisor held the agent's pipe and an IPC channel to the controller, so a dead controller (ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED) killed supervisor and agent and lost finished cli results (T8). Plan 6.2 built and proved the replacement: crash matrix through real bwrap and real fgos run, process-containment CI green on Linux, Windows and macOS, full suite green. Review threshold: an agent result lost after a controller or supervisor death, or a containment escape seen outside the named escapes.

decisions.text: D-ADR0057: Git is one foundation component (fgos-git, Rust live core) that owns every git mutation and its recovery -- typed operations (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication), no public git(args) door, a hash-chained file WAL under the git common dir as the sole recovery authority, one target attempt per operation, 4.3-R locks reused (20 -> 40 -> 50, branch refs under worktree-admin 40), Node reaching Rust through one combined N-API addon shared with fgos-event-store, and the refs/fgos/* Publication port that Event Store calls; the three parallel git cores are deleted in the same release that switches their callers.
decisions.rationale: Three parallel git cores and the event log in the work tree caused most git and lock incidents (git lessons catalogue, 234 entries); the owner wants one authority done once. Architecture council wf-run-1792246479016-19b58eab, owner answers 2026-10-17 23:18, proofs and two re-checks 2026-10-18 (docs/platform/git/spec.md section 19).

decisions.text: D-ADR0058: Git publication recovery after a crashed seal (adds to D-ADR0057) -- a PublicationCas left at TargetAttempt without outcome does not block later seals of its ref: a later operation id under the same publication authority may proceed, and the old one closes record-only with the terminal outcome of Git spec section 10 rule 4a once a later durable winning receipt exists, the old domain is proven gone through the holder-lock predecessor admission, and no backend native lock remains; Publication git children always run borrowed under event-seal with hooks off; the old CAS is never run again.
decisions.rationale: A seal crash at the wrong moment would leave recovery-required forever and block every later seal, WAL compaction and rollback (event store plan M3). Model check and real-git re-check 2026-10-18 (docs/platform/git/spec.md section 19).

decisions.text: D-ADR0059: The run supervisor watches herdr rounds through terminal-control, no longer the controller -- a herdr-spawn seat is a terminal-mode attempt of the one executeAssignment door (envelope v3 mode terminal, Rust supervisor and gate); the supervisor drives the pane through terminal-control by attempt id, the gate in the pane receives the attempt lock and cwd lease over SCM_RIGHTS, checks the peer uid and gives the agent the foreground tty; deadline, settle and pane close survive a dead controller (orphan-result, adopt, release-slot); release-slot closes the pane only on a clean end and otherwise keeps it; the attempt writer id is att-<attemptId> in both modes; the controller polling loop, herdr reconcile, liveness and the herdr part of the reaper are deleted
decisions.rationale: The controller owned the herdr round loop (poll, deadline, settle, pane close): when it died all three were lost (T8 hB/hC/hD), and the reaper patch with pane ids in the home marker only treated the symptom and once nearly removed a live worker's home. Proven on real herdr: five CLIs settled pass, controller SIGKILL/SIGTERM and timeout rounds settle and keep or close the pane correctly, supervisor kill before and after the agent start ends as abandoned-not-started or orphan-result and adopt closes it.

decisions.text: D-ADR0061: RUL104 better, not bigger -- every audit, review or hardening of existing code makes what exists better (more stable, faster, lighter, simpler code; clearer, explicit, easier and more flexible APIs, signatures and contracts) within the existing scope and never bigger: no new feature, layer or mechanism; a changed contract moves every caller and deletes the old path in the same change (L10); a feature is added only when truly worth it: every feature idea goes into one separate section of the report with its reason (real problem, evidence) and benefit, and is built only after the owner chooses it
decisions.rationale: Owner statement 2026-10-18 when assigning the low-level hardening lane: 'trong phạm vi code đang có ... tuyệt đối không mở rộng scope (scope creep), chỉ tốt hơn không bự hơn' and 'Chỉ thêm tính năng nếu nó thật sự đáng ... gom tất cả những ý tưởng cần thêm vào một chỗ ... giải thích rõ lý do và lợi ích'. It blocks an audit that answers a weakness by adding a flag, layer or mechanism, and feature ideas slipping into the fix list unchosen.

decisions.text: D-ADR0060: A dead controller leaves a settled attempt and a unit awaiting an explicit --resume; automatic resume is a named deferral -- Ctrl-C/SIGTERM of fgos run asks the supervisor to cancel the delivered attempt, waits dispatch.cancelWaitMs for its receipt and exits 130/143; --resume asks adopt first: a closed attempt with a result is used as is and the agent never runs again, after a cancelled or abandoned attempt the unit runs again in a new attempt that points back to it, a running or legacy attempt is refused by name, a second concurrent resume is refused resume-in-progress, and a bound attempt is never given a second supervisor; recover gains adopt and abandon-legacy; runs from before the supervisor stuck running are settled abandoned-legacy by doctor only when every recorded pid is dead; binding present with a dead gate stays gate-lost (fail closed)
decisions.rationale: Controller death lost the attempt result (resume started over in runs/02), recover parked on result-N.json, and T8 left running attempts nobody cleaned. Proven by the crash matrix of r6 9.7 in direct and terminal mode, the resume and cancel tests, T8 rerun (8 cases incl. real herdr), and a full suite of 8190 tests on the integration tip.

decisions.text: D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger): a Workflow is an operating guide plus constraints, not a script. The agent proposes the order; the Workflow case admits each activity against its ledger and records progress. Narrows 0048 §2 (agent proposes, case admits and records) and 0049 §4 (Workflow is the single authority for admission and the progress record, not the chooser of order); 0048 §1, §3, §4 and 0049 §1-3 stay.
decisions.rationale: 0049 ended authority sprawl but also took ordering judgement from the agent, against the hard-outside soft-inside vision and the owner direction of 2026-10-18; 0 of 89 stored runs were coding/feature; lead chain 6.4 slipped prose-only rules three times while machine guards held. Flexibility goes to the agent, constraints to machine guards: closed catalog of six MUST checks, N1 fail-closed authority on writing dispatch into a case-bound worktree, AdmissionPort owned by Execution Core and implemented by Workflow, Shape C for advance, JSONL ledger hardened in place. Owner 2026-10-19: 08:46 N1; 12:20 Shape C, Playbook proposer, refuse confined nested writes, N1 limited to the two doors, no Event Store; 12:32 spec approved; 12:35 feature ideas F1-F7, F9, F11, F12.

decisions.text: D-ADR0071 (model pool B1): a seat walks its tier's declared family order after a failure (runner.tierFallback, capability prefer only narrows), cross-family fallback is on within the tier (doer tiers to cheap equivalent families, flagship/frontier to premium ones), accounts rotate in declared order (same pool first), lease/state/quarantine are keyed by pool, an account pins as pool/account, and a missing tier cell refuses tier-cell-missing. Partly supersedes runner record 0051 item 1 and 0058 items 2, 3, 6.
decisions.rationale: Per-capability fallback order could not say which family to try at a tier, least-lease spread burned quotas unpredictably, and family-keyed lease state mixed pools. Owner answers 2026-10-19 23:07 and 23:20 (problem-261017-0022). Reversal: back to least-lease if one account keeps hitting its quota while others idle; tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent.
